summary: Lolo National Forest L-4 lookout house on a 30-foot pole tower, built 1938 near Lolo, Montana, and destroyed 1980; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 lookout house on a 30-foot pole tower
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1980; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Montana list marks it as gone

events.note: Firelookout.com says built in 1938; the state form says a 1931-plan L-4 lookout house was erected on a pole tower in 1938
Firelookout.com names Mrs. Robert Haugen as known lookout personnel for 1962
Firelookout.com says the tower was destroyed in 1980; the page gives no cause

notes_for_editor: The 1938 build year agrees between firelookout.com and the state National Register form (which cites Kresek's Fire Lookouts of the Northwest). The 1980 destruction and the 1962 staff entry rest on firelookout.com alone. The 1962 name is a private person from a lookout history page; check before publishing. height_m 9.1 is the 30-foot pole converted. The Trailforks Mormon Peak Road page returned HTTP 403 and is not cited. Mineral Peak in the state form is a different lookout (Lolo NF, standing), not this one. Two WebSearch calls used. Fact-check 2026-10-10: facts.access removed; its level 'public' was not supported by any source, and no source says whether the site is open.
